eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus on 20°C as the highest temperature in Helsinki on August 8 reflects real-time observations and forecasts from the Finnish Meteorological Institute confirming this peak under moderate southwesterly winds, partly cloudy skies, and minimal solar heating.** Daytime readings climbed steadily from morning lows near 17°C to a maximum of 20°C by late afternoon, with forecasts holding at or below this level through evening. This aligns with typical early-August conditions in southern Finland, where average highs hover around 20°C amid Atlantic-influenced flow that limits extremes. The near-100% market-implied probability accounts for the narrow uncertainty range in official models (±1°C) and the low likelihood of localized spikes. A realistic challenge would require unexpected clearing skies or a wind shift allowing brief additional warming before sunset, though current data show little potential for deviation.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/fi/vantaa/EFHK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Finnish Meteorological Institute and other agencies indicate a daytime high near 20–21°C for Helsinki on August 9 under sunny intervals and moderate westerly winds, consistent with late-summer cooling trends and the absence of strong high-pressure systems that could drive further warming. Coastal sea-breeze effects and typical August climatology, with average highs declining from July peaks, reinforce this range and limit upside potential above 23°C. Traders have concentrated implied probability on 22°C (55.5%) and 21°C (31%), reflecting minor model optimism and recent stable observations, while lower odds for extremes align with low historical variance this time of year and the proximity to resolution.

Subtropical monsoon conditions and typical August heat, averaging 33°C highs but frequently peaking near 37–38°C, support this outlook amid limited cooling from cloud cover or precipitation. This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/fr/bonneuil-en-france/LFPB.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from European forecasting agencies points to a high-pressure ridge sustaining mostly clear skies and light winds over northern France, supporting a daytime maximum in Paris around 31–33°C on August 10. Ensemble runs show modest spread, with some solutions reaching 35°C if subsidence strengthens, while others cap near 30°C amid slightly higher boundary-layer moisture. This range aligns with climatological August peaks near 25–28°C but reflects the current warm anomaly persisting after earlier summer heat. Traders have concentrated probability on 31–33°C outcomes, reflecting the narrow uncertainty window two days ahead and limited upside risk from the latest guidance. Updated runs from Météo-France and ECMWF are expected to refine the final range before resolution.
